sections.content: St. Louis, Missouri is quietly one of the best cities in America for real estate investors. Low home prices, a diverse rental market, and consistent demand make it a standout market whether you are a first-time wholesaler or a seasoned flipper building a portfolio. If you are just getting started, check out our Real Estate Investing for Beginners guide before diving in. For everyone else, this article covers everything you need to know about finding real estate deals in St. Louis MO — from neighborhood breakdowns to deal types to tips for out-of-state investors.
St. Louis Real Estate Market Overview

St. Louis sits at the crossroads of the Midwest with a metro population of around 2.8 million people. The city has a long history of manufacturing, healthcare, and education — anchored by major employers like Boeing, Centene Corporation, Washington University, and BJC HealthCare. That employment base keeps rental demand stable even when other markets cool off. As of 2024, the median home price in the city of St. Louis proper is roughly $165,000, compared to a national median of around $420,000. The broader St. Louis metro area sits around $245,000. Those numbers mean your entry costs are dramatically lower here than in coastal markets, and your margins as an investor are much easier to protect.

One important thing to understand about St. Louis is the city-county split. The City of St. Louis is an independent city — it is not part of St. Louis County. This affects property taxes, school districts, and neighborhood dynamics in ways that matter to investors. Generally speaking, St. Louis County suburbs offer more stability and appreciation, while the city offers deeper discounts, higher cash-flow potential, and more wholesale opportunities. Smart investors learn to work both sides of that line.
Best Neighborhoods for Real Estate Investors in St. Louis

Not every zip code in St. Louis is created equal. The city has a patchwork of neighborhoods ranging from highly revitalized areas to blocks still recovering from decades of disinvestment. Knowing where to focus makes all the difference between a great deal and a money pit. Explore the full breakdown of investor activity and deal flow at our St. Louis MO market hub.
Top Neighborhoods for Fix and Flip

items: Shaw and Tower Grove South: Historic brick homes with strong ARVs in the $250,000–$350,000 range. Buyers love the walkability and proximity to Tower Grove Park.
Maplewood and Richmond Heights: Just inside St. Louis County, these suburbs have seen rapid appreciation. Flipped homes routinely sell above $300,000.
Benton Park and Soulard: Some of the oldest neighborhoods in the city with loyal buyer pools. Renovated properties here sell fast at premiums of 20–30% over nearby comps.
Clayton and Webster Groves: Higher-end suburbs ideal for luxury flips. Entry costs are higher but ARVs regularly exceed $500,000 on fully renovated properties.

sections.content: Top Neighborhoods for Buy-and-Hold Rentals

items: Affton and Mehlville: South county suburbs with steady working-class rental demand, low vacancy rates, and homes that can be purchased in the $120,000–$180,000 range.
Ferguson and Florissant: North county markets offering some of the strongest gross rental yields in the metro. Single-family homes under $100,000 renting for $900–$1,200 per month are still findable.
Lemay and Oakville: Value-oriented south county submarkets with solid schools, low crime, and consistent tenant demand from healthcare and trade workers.
University City: Near Washington University, this area supports strong rental demand from students and young professionals, with multifamily performing especially well.

sections.content: Pro Tip: Before making an offer on any St. Louis property, always verify the taxing district carefully. City of St. Louis and St. Louis County have very different tax structures, and some neighborhoods have additional TIF or special assessment districts that can significantly affect your net operating income on a rental or your carrying costs on a flip.
Types of Real Estate Deals Available in St. Louis
Wholesale Deals

St. Louis is a wholesaler's market. High volumes of distressed, vacant, and probate properties create a steady stream of off-market opportunities. Motivated sellers include out-of-state heirs, landlords exiting the market, and homeowners dealing with deferred maintenance on aging brick construction. Assignment fees of $10,000–$25,000 are common on city properties, while suburban wholesale deals can yield $15,000–$40,000 or more depending on the ARV. If you are new to the wholesale process, start with our Wholesaling Real Estate for Beginners guide to understand the fundamentals before building your pipeline. Before you lock up any deal, run your numbers through our free Wholesale Deal Calculator to make sure your offer makes sense for both you and your buyer.
Fix and Flip Opportunities

St. Louis flippers benefit from some of the most affordable renovation targets in the country. A distressed brick bungalow in Benton Park might cost $60,000 to acquire and $70,000 to renovate, with an ARV of $220,000 — leaving a gross profit of $90,000 before carrying costs and fees. That kind of margin is nearly impossible to find in Denver, Nashville, or Phoenix right now. The key is accurate ARV estimation. Use our free ARV Calculator to pull realistic after-repair values before you commit to any purchase price. Overestimating ARV is the number one mistake that kills flip deals in this market.
Long-Term Rentals and BRRRR Strategy

The BRRRR strategy — Buy, Rehab, Rent, Refinance, Repeat — works exceptionally well in St. Louis. Low acquisition costs mean you can often pull out most or all of your invested capital after a cash-out refinance once the property is stabilized. Average rents in St. Louis city range from $850 for a basic one-bedroom to $1,400 or more for a renovated three-bedroom in a desirable neighborhood. In the suburbs, a renovated three-bedroom in Florissant or Affton can command $1,200–$1,600 per month with minimal vacancy. Cash-on-cash returns of 8–14% are achievable for investors who buy right and manage efficiently.
How to Find Off-Market Deals in St. Louis

The best real estate deals in St. Louis MO are rarely listed on the MLS. Most high-margin opportunities come from off-market channels where motivated sellers haven't yet been exposed to retail buyer competition. Our full guide on How to Find Off-Market Real Estate Deals covers every strategy in depth, but here are the most effective tactics specific to the St. Louis market.

items: Probate court records: St. Louis City and County both have active probate courts processing inherited properties. Filing for notice as a creditor or monitoring court dockets gives you early access to motivated estate sellers.

Driving for dollars: Vacant and distressed properties are concentrated in specific corridors in north and south city. Physically driving neighborhoods to identify neglected brick homes and tracing ownership through the assessor's website is still one of the most reliable lead generation tactics.
Tax delinquency lists: Both the city and county publish tax delinquent property lists. Owners who are behind on taxes are often highly motivated to sell before the property goes to a tax sale.

Direct mail to absentee owners: Out-of-state landlords in zip codes like 63115, 63120, and 63136 are frequently looking for exit strategies. A consistent direct mail campaign targeting absentee owners in these zip codes can generate reliable deal flow.

Building relationships with local wholesalers: St. Louis has an active wholesale community. Attending local REIA meetings and connecting with established wholesalers gives you access to their deal flow, often before properties hit buyers lists.

Tips for Out-of-State Investors Targeting St. Louis

St. Louis is one of the most accessible Midwest markets for remote investing, but there are a few things out-of-state investors consistently get wrong. Understanding these pitfalls upfront will save you from expensive mistakes. Learning how to analyze real estate deals rigorously is especially important when you cannot physically walk every block yourself.

items: Hire a local property manager before you buy, not after. St. Louis has a fragmented rental market and tenant laws that favor renters in some situations. A good local PM will help you avoid bad tenants, navigate maintenance issues on older brick construction, and handle city housing inspections.

Understand the occupancy permit process. The City of St. Louis requires a occupancy permit for both rental properties and property transfers. This inspection process can delay closings and reveal hidden issues — budget time and money for it.

Do not skip boots-on-the-ground inspection. Even if you are investing remotely, pay for a thorough independent inspection by someone who knows brick construction. Foundation issues, tuckpointing needs, and old sewer lateral problems are common and expensive.

Focus on specific zip codes rather than the whole metro. Zip codes like 63118, 63104, and 63116 have very different risk profiles than 63136 or 63147. Build your market knowledge neighborhood by neighborhood.

sections.content: St. Louis Market Trends to Watch in 2024

Several trends are shaping the opportunity landscape for investors in the St. Louis market right now. First, rising interest rates have softened retail buyer demand, which is actually good news for investors — less competition at purchase and more tenant demand as would-be buyers stay in the rental market longer. Second, several north and south city neighborhoods are showing early signs of gentrification, with coffee shops, restaurants, and new construction beginning to appear in areas that were distressed just five years ago. Getting into these transitional areas early can mean significant appreciation on top of strong cash flow. Third, the city's ongoing vacancy remediation programs are both a challenge and an opportunity — properties in certain demolition target areas need to move fast, but savvy investors who can close quickly on those deals often find the deepest discounts available anywhere in the metro.
